B-spline fillets/blends typical of cast structural knuckle arms

primarySuggestion.name: Ductile (nodular) cast iron GJS500-7
primarySuggestion.reasoning: Steering knuckles are safety-critical suspension components almost universally produced as ductile iron sand castings or forged steel, never thin-wall die-cast aluminium, due to fatigue/impact loading. The 52-undercut geometry, thick non-uniform walls (1.4-46.7mm), bosses and bearing bore all match a sand-cast ductile-iron knuckle machined on bore/hub/mounting faces. No aluminium signal (uniform 2-4mm HPDC wall, filename hint) is present, so per guidance the default for a solid drivetrain/suspension part is steel/ductile iron rather than aluminium.

processRecommendations.reasoning: User-forced cast_and_machine; ductile-iron sand casting is the standard high-volume route for steering knuckles, with subsequent machining of bearing bore, mounting holes and mating faces.
Feasible for aluminium alternative but not selected given steel/iron material choice.
Forged steel knuckles are an alternative production route offering higher fatigue strength but higher tooling/die cost; less favoured for the freeform cored geometry seen here.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Extensive undercuts require multiple side-cores/pulls in the sand mould, increasing pattern complexity and scrap risk from core shift.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Consolidate undercuts where possible or plan the pattern with pre-defined core prints and locating features.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Very thin local sections adjacent to much thicker bosses (mean 23mm) risk misruns, cold shuts and porosity in sand casting.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Increase minimum wall to >4mm or redesign as a rib rather than a thin web; add chills/risers at thin-to-thick transitions.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Holes are cast-undersized or solid and finished by drilling/reaming/tapping in 3 setups, adding cycle time and requiring accurate as-cast datum locating.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Cast clean locating bosses/pads for fixturing and consider casting pilot holes to reduce drilling stock.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Bore is a critical, tightly toleranced feature that must be finish-bored/ground after casting; as-cast ovality and core shift will affect stock allowance uniformity.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Add generous machining allowance (2-3mm/side) and finish-bore in single setup off common datums.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Large proportion of zero-draft planar faces increases pattern lift resistance and risk of sand tear-out.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Apply minimum 1-2° draft to non-machined faces where functionally acceptable.

dfmIssues.description: 52 undercut faces demand multiple sand cores or side-pulls, raising pattern cost and risk of core shift causing wall-thickness variance.
dfmIssues.impact: Increases pattern tooling cost (~15-25%) and scrap rate (target <2% vs typical 5-8% with poor core control).
dfmIssues.fix: Re-orient part or simplify geometry to consolidate undercuts into fewer, larger cores with robust core prints.

dfmIssues.description: Local wall far below the 4-6mm sand-casting practical minimum for ductile iron risks incomplete fill and cold shut defects.
dfmIssues.impact: Casting scrap/rework, potential in-service fatigue failure risk if defect undetected.
dfmIssues.fix: Thicken minimum sections to ≥4mm or convert thin web to a cast rib with generous fillets.

dfmIssues.description: Critical bore (Ø63-88mm equivalent) must be bored to tight tolerance from an as-cast surface with core-shift induced eccentricity.
dfmIssues.impact: Extra roughing pass or larger machining stock required, adding ~0.05-0.1hr/part machining time.
dfmIssues.fix: Add 2-3mm/side uniform machining allowance and use the bore itself as a locating datum in the casting pattern.

dfmIssues.description: 14 holes plus tapped features must be drilled/reamed/tapped after casting in up to 3 setups, adding non-value cycle time.
dfmIssues.impact: Adds ~7min/part drilling + setup overhead, ~10-15% of total machining cost.
dfmIssues.fix: Cast pilot/cored holes to near-finish size and combine hole operations into fewer setups using shared datums.

dfmIssues.description: 102 faces show zero draft, increasing pattern withdrawal force and sand tear risk.
dfmIssues.impact: Higher scrap/rework rate on non-critical cosmetic faces.
dfmIssues.fix: Add 1-2° draft on all non-machined faces during pattern design.

analysis.aiExplanation: This is a right-hand steering knuckle, a safety-critical suspension component. Its sparse fill ratio (0.0615) combined with thick, non-uniform wall sections, 124 cylindrical bore/boss faces, 52 undercuts and a large bearing bore is characteristic of a sand-cast ductile-iron part machined on its functional interfaces (hub bore, ball-joint/tie-rod holes, caliper bracket faces). Per the forced cast_and_machine process and 200,000 units/year volume, a durable metal matchplate sand pattern (£17k, ~500k-shot life) feeding an automated green-sand ductile-iron foundry line is the standard high-volume route, followed by 3-setup CNC machining (5-axis for the undercut/hub faces, then drilling/tapping) totalling ~0.296hr cycle plus 0.75hr setup. Aluminium was deliberately not selected despite lower weight, because steering knuckles require the fatigue/impact toughness of ductile iron or forged steel and show none of the thin uniform HPDC wall signals that would indicate an aluminium die-cast design.
analysisLimitations: Material (ductile iron vs forged steel vs aluminium) inferred from part type and geometry only; no drawing/BOM material callout was provided.
Cavity count and pattern life for sand casting are rule-of-thumb estimates for 200k/yr automated foundry, not derived from geometry.
Cost range is a parametric estimate; actual costs depend on foundry yield, local labour/energy rates and casting quality achieved.

processRecommendations.reasoning: selected by the deterministic rules for this commodity

dfmIssues.description: Non-uniform sections (heavy:thin ≈ 34.4:1) — Heavy sections solidify last and shrink, drawing porosity/sink at the hot spot.
dfmIssues.fix: Even out wall thickness, core out heavy bosses, add fillets to taper transitions, or feed the hot spot with a riser/chill.

dfmIssues.description: Draft -1° below recommended 0.5° — Insufficient draft galls the die/pattern, raises ejection force and accelerates tool wear (or breaks the sand mould).
dfmIssues.fix: Add ≥ 0.5° draft on all as-cast vertical walls; deep pockets need more. Investment casting can run near-zero draft if this is fixed.

deterministicAnalysis.aiExplanation:
Derived deterministically for cast_and_machine from the measured geometry. No AI call was made; every figure below is arithmetic on a measurement or a library lookup, and each states its own basis.

Still open (1):
  • What is this part made of? — A CAD file carries shape, not substance. We measured 356 cm³ exactly, but the same solid weighs 0.96 kg in aluminium and 2.79 kg in steel. Nothing in the geometry distinguishes them, and guessing wrong moves the material cost several-fold.
analysisLimitations: Unanswered: What is this part made of?

DFM checks ran against the measured geometry. Checks that need a drawing callout — tolerances, which face is critical, whether a weld line is in a load path — did not run, so this list is a floor and not a ceiling.
